text: Good morning, Pip! The water is so calm today.
Ollie, look! They are all linked up.
They're holding hands, even while they sleep!
Why do otters hold hands?
Let's find out!
Maybe they're cold! Or maybe they're best friends!
Ollie, I think Bean is floating away.
Oh no. I swam off without you, Bean.
Look. Now you're not drifting at all.
Hmm. Is that why otters hold hands?
Even the baby is holding on.
Hold hands? That sounds slow. I've got a faster way!
Gus, your faster ways always go wrong.
Not this time! I'll just lie down and stay right here.
You won't hold on to anything?
Nope! Naps are easy. Watch me.
What if we try it the careful way?
Good idea, Pip. Let's watch Gus first. Then we ask Gran Mari.
Ollie, he's drifting away!
Gus! Gus, wake up! You're floating away!
Hey! Where did everybody go?
Did you float away, Gus?
No! I went for a swim. On purpose!
But you were asleep.
I was swimming in my sleep. Very fast. Everyone does it.
The water moved you, and nothing held you.
It was only a little bit. It doesn't count!
We need help. Let's ask Gran Mari.
Well now, a damp seagull and a worried otter. What's all this?
Gran Mari, why do otters hold hands?
Oh, that is a good question, Ollie. Let's find out together.
This bowl is a pretend sea. These leaves are pretend otters.
This string is pretend paws. Watch the water, and watch closely.
They're drifting! The loose ones are drifting apart!
The tied leaves stay together!
The sea is always moving, even when the otters sleep. So they hold paws, and nothing pulls them apart.
So if I'd held on to something, I wouldn't have drifted?
Well now, what do you think happens next?
The loose leaves keep drifting, and the tied leaves stay close!
Try it at home! Fill a bowl with water. Float four leaves on it. Tie two leaves together with a soft string.
Now swirl the water gently. Watch the loose leaves drift apart. Watch the tied leaves stay together.
Gus, come float with us. There's room.
I fibbed before. I wasn't swimming. I was drifting.
I'm sorry I said it didn't count.
Thanks for telling us the truth, Gus.
Hold!
Phew! I'm not going anywhere. Thanks, friends.
We stayed together all by ourselves.
Time for my Wonder Pocket! Three things we learned.
One. The sea is always moving, even at night.
Two. Otters hold paws so they do not drift apart.
Three. Holding on keeps friends together.
And one kind thing to try today. Hold a friend's hand.
Bye, everybody! Next time, I'll hold on too!
